title: Allocation granularity and hybrid pool experimentation
content:
Summary:

This doc captures a sequence of experiments and field observations exploring how allocation granularity and a hybrid allocation pool (slab + large-block) affect fragmentation and OOM patterns in the serving runtime. Motivation arose from two customer incidents (RINF-1987) where sustained multimodel workloads triggered unexpected peak OOMs despite apparent average utilization headroom. The hypothesis: a combination of small persistent allocations (kvcache, attention buffers) plus variable large activations creates interleaved holes that our current single-strategy mempool amplifies.

Goals:
- Characterize how allocation size distribution (micro = <2KB, small = 2KB-128KB, medium = 128KB-8MB, large = >8MB) correlates with fragmentation metrics and cudaMalloc retry rates.
- Prototype a hybrid pool allocator that splits requests by size class into slab (fixed-size small bins) and chunked large-block arenas to reduce internal fragmentation and improve coalescing for long-lived buffers.
- Measure end-to-end impact on successful allocation latency, retry frequency, and observed tail latency in token generation SLOs.

Telemetry and signals used:
- per-request allocation histogram (size, lifetime tag), with percentiles and bucket counts.
- cudaMalloc / cudaMallocAsync call counts and latencies (success/fail), including retry traces and caller stacks (sampled).
- GPU resident bytes and free regions map (approx from allocator metadata).
- kvcache growth events and eviction timestamps.
- OOM/Allocation-failure logs with preallocation snapshot attached (last 10s allocations).
- Token-level tail latency, especially 99.9th pct in multi-tenant pools.

Reproduction notes (local lab):
- Use dedicated test rig: A100 80GB, driver 535.x, CUDA 12.1. Runtime built with allocator debug hooks enabled.
- Workload: mixed-profile replay of production traces (2025-10) with two model families: encoder-only embedding model (~2B) and a 70B decoder-only chat model.
- Config: 4 concurrent sessions, batch size distribution p(batch=1)=0.65 p(batch=2)=0.25 p(batch>=4)=0.1. Sequence lengths sampled from production distribution (max 2048). KV cache usage enabled for decoder model.
- Run duration 30 minutes to allow slow drift/reservoir effects.

Key findings:
1) Allocation-size clustering creates long-lived small holes.
- Small allocations from completion/composition stacks (token logits, temp activation slices) had median lifetime ~200ms but occurred at very high rate. Large allocations (activations, kv cache) had lifetimes orders of magnitude larger (seconds-minutes). When the pool served both with similar grain, free lists became fragmented: a large contiguous free region was broken into many small free nodes, preventing satisfied large-block allocations and triggering cudaMalloc fallback/retry.

2) cudaMallocAsync reduces immediate latency but does not magically avoid fragmentation.
- Async allocator helps reduce per-call latency variance, but we still saw increase in retry rates when fragmentation prevented contiguous block placement. The async backend defers physical free coalescing and the default slab heuristics did not coalesce aggressively enough.

3) Bump-on-demand for ephemeral micro-allocations reduced small-allocation amplification.
- Implemented a per-stream bump bump-pointer (fast single-threaded arena) for micro allocations (<2KB) that are known to be short-lived (annotated by caller). This eliminated >60% of small freelist churn and improved average allocation latency for small requests. It also lowered fragmentation entropy measured by free-block-size variance.

4) Hybrid slab + chunked arenas improved large allocation success rate.
- When requests >8MB were delegated to chunked arenas that allocate from coalescing virtual ranges (and use cudaMalloc to map large contiguous chunks), large alloc success increased by ~4x under stress. Slab continued to serve small/small-medium requests.

5) Eviction/coalescing timing matters more than pool size.
- Increasing reserve pool size by 10% only deferred OOM; the fragmentation pattern reappeared. Aggressive coalescing pass (background defrag every 500ms) reduced peak failures but introduced CPU overhead and occasional visible tail spikes. Tradeoff space: background defrag frequency vs CPU/latency jitter.

Experiments run (brief):
- EXP-A: baseline mempool (single freelist), run replay -> observed 42 cudaMalloc retries in 30m, 3 OOM events.
- EXP-B: bump-pointer for micro allocations + baseline -> retries 16, OOM 1.
- EXP-C: hybrid slab + chunked arenas (no background defrag) -> retries 6, OOM 0, slight increase in average allocation latency for large (5ms -> 8ms).
- EXP-D: hybrid + aggressive background defrag (500ms pass) -> retries 2, OOM 0, CPU thread utilization +12% and occasional 99.9th latency spike at defrag moment.

Instrumentation snippets used (pseudo):
- Allocation trace line: "ts,req_id,size,lifetime_est_ms,alloc_kind,stream_id,caller_tag"
- Free map query: run allocator --dump-free-map | python analyse_free_map.py --heatmap
- cudaMalloc retry logging patch: instrument cuda_check_retry() to emit sample stack and mem map.

Practical mitigations proposed:
1) Ship bump-pointer micro-allocator for ephemeral per-request allocations (configurable opt-in per model). Low risk, minimal change surface.
2) Implement size-class routing: requests <=128KB -> slab bins; 128KB-8MB -> medium pool; >8MB -> chunked arenas. Parameterizable thresholds (we tuned as above).
3) Add a gentle background coalescer tuned to avoid SLO interference: run when queue depth low, limit CPU to 25% of a core, pause during high p99 tail.
4) Pre-reserve large-chunk pools for heavy KV-use customers: allow customer-config to pin x GB chunked pool to avoid cross-tenant fragmentation.
5) Improve telemetry: expose per-tenant fragmentation index (free-node-size-entropy) and allocation-failure susceptibility score. Alert when susceptibility > threshold.

Risks and open questions:
- Defrag overhead: the defrag thread can cause jitter; need better heuristics to avoid running during high token emit periods. Possibly integrate with the scheduler to run during natural idle windows.
- Cross-stream reads/writes: bump-pointer arenas are per-stream; some callers currently share buffers across streams. We need to audit call sites and add safe fallbacks.
- GPU driver/version idiosyncrasies: some driver versions coalesce virtual ranges differently; run matrix across drivers.
- Interaction with CUDA UVM & MIG: untested in our experiments — customer fleets with MIG slices may behave differently.

Next steps (practical roadmap):
1) Land bump-pointer micro-allocator (PR referenced) behind a feature flag. Run canary on dedicated pools that previously saw small-allocation churn. (owner: Priya)
2) Prototype hybrid allocator in canary branch; measure 72h runs on multi-model traces and compare OOM and retry rates. (owner: Liu)
3) Add fragmentation telemetry and an alert rule to platform monitoring. (owner: Ethan)
4) Run driver-compat matrix (Cuda 11.8, 12.1, 12.2) across A10, A100, H100 hardware in lab. (owner: Samir)
5) Draft runbook for customer success: mitigation steps (reduce batch size, enable small-alloc bump, restart workers to coalesce). (owner: Priya/Ethan)

Notes to reviewers:
- The hybrid approach is not a silver bullet; it reduces failure rates in observed traces but needs careful tuning for different workload mixes.
- The bump-pointer change requires audit of shared-buffer patterns (we included a lint check to catch non-localized buffer-sharing).
- Attached traces and CSV dumps are in linked artifacts; see PR for microbench scripts.

Quick checklist before rolling out to production:
- [ ] Comprehensive unit tests for allocator invariants (free map correctness).
- [ ] Stress test with long-running KV-growth scenarios (simulate 24h).
- [ ] Failure-injection harness: force fragmented free map and assert graceful fallback to reserved pool instead of crash.
- [ ] Docs for ops: tuning knobs, expected telemetry signals, and rollback steps.

Appendix (short):
- Useful commands: 
  - "./runtime --alloc-debug --dump-free-map > freemap.json"
  - "python scripts/alloc_histogram.py traces/2025-10/replay.log --bucket=4k"
  - "nvprof/ Nsight snapshots used to correlate big-block placement vs stream activity"

End.
